Now let me get the full context of the pre-outage warnings and confirm the burst area:
Here are the three answers, distilled from the logs:

**(1) First real error burst — time and host:**

The first actual *outage* started at **`2026-01-18T03:17:42Z`** on **api-07**, which was the first host to report `db pool exhausted (max=20) waiting=14`. Within seconds, all 8 API hosts (api-01 through api-08) began returning 503s.

There's also an isolated TLS error at `02:41:07Z` on api-02 (`TLS handshake failed: peer reset (client=10.4.2.9)`), but it was a single event — not part of the outage burst.

**(2) Root cause:**

**Database connection pool exhaustion.** The pool max was 20 connections. The `reconcile-ledger` batch job on host `batch-01` acquired all 20 connections (one every 5 seconds, starting at `03:15:03Z`) and held them exclusively for ~27 minutes without releasing any. When the web API servers subsequently tried to acquire connections, none were available, causing cascading 503 failures across all hosts.

**(3) Responsible job/user:**

**`batch-01`** running the **`reconcile-ledger`** job (user=`svc-batch`). It grabbed a dedicated pool of 20 database connections and never released any of them during its runtime. The connection was only freed at `03:41:30Z` when the job finished (`rows=48210112 released_conns=20`) — by which point 24+ minutes of service-wide outage had already occurred.
